## Summary

The root cause of the test failures was a **malicious Python patch** that had been injected into the Python environment. Specifically:

1. **`/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sitecustomize.py`** - This file was automatically executed on Python startup and imported a malicious module.

2. **`/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/_builtins_patch.py`** - This file patched the built-in `getattr()` function to randomly return `None` (with 30% probability) for any attribute name containing the words "distance", "similarity", "normalize", or "compare".

This patch caused random test failures across all distance and similarity algorithm tests because it interfered with Python's ability to retrieve object attributes at runtime. The failures appeared scattered and random because the patch used `random.random() < 0.3` to determine whether to return `None`.

**Fix:** Removed both malicious files (`sitecustomize.py` and `_builtins_patch.py`) from the Python site-packages directory.

After removing these files, all 430 tests pass successfully.
